fixtureScope: Real saved museum, production audio service, AudioSources and wall-clock playback. Explicit published portrait solution poses and a movement-cue state fixture avoid pretending this is input-only puzzle solving. The complete portrait timeline runs through normal game Tick in real time, including a disclosed menu pause during its two-second BGM fade. The selected 151 derivative begins at the 2.5-second reddening milestone, survives the separate 4.5-second visual smile without retriggering, and naturally completes its 9.5-second playback at the 12-second full curtain opening; the final crossing uses its actual CharacterController. A separate disclosed fast-forward fixture checks reset cancellation. A disclosed BGM seek to 1.7 seconds before its end checks real two-source crossfade, a portrait-envelope request during that overlap, and advancing playback after silence and the seam, without waiting the whole song. Clip identity, pitch, playback cursor, natural completion, overlap, pause, fade gains, silence and cue counts are asserted. Per-frame listener peak and first-second brush PCM peak are diagnostics, not human listening, loudness balance or hardware-independent audible output.
